rationale: Body mass and flipper length have a strong morphometric relationship and are a common exploratory comparison in the dataset.
Body mass differs substantially across the three penguin species.
Flipper length differs substantially across penguin species.
Bill length is one of the morphological measurements that distinguishes species.
Daily rental demand changes materially over the 731-date observation window, making a time-series view useful.
Rental demand is meaningfully associated with temperature.
Humidity is a weather variable with a meaningful relationship to rental demand.
UCI defines season as categorical, and daily rental demand differs across seasons.
UCI defines weather situation as categorical, and rental demand differs across weather conditions.
Survival status differs substantially by sex. The intended visualization is survival rate by sex rather than the reverse orientation.
Passenger class is a core survival-related factor. The intended view is survival rate by passenger class.
Age distributions are useful to compare between survivors and non-survivors.
Passenger fares differ strongly across the three passenger classes.
Passenger fare has a distinctly uneven distribution that is useful to inspect.
The outcome of a previous marketing campaign is a natural and decision-relevant grouping for current term-deposit subscription rate.
Occupation is a core customer attribute and subscription rates can meaningfully differ across job categories.
Education level is a core customer attribute and is useful to compare against subscription rate.
The contact month can capture substantial campaign timing differences in subscription rate.
Average yearly account balance is an important financial measure to compare between clients who did and did not subscribe.
Age distributions are useful to compare between subscribers and non-subscribers.
